0.long_answer: Mutations in the CLCN7 gene have been most commonly associated with autosomal dominant osteopetrosis type II. This form of osteopetrosis, also known as Albers-Schönberg disease, is characterized by a dominant negative effect of the mutated chloride channel protein, leading to abnormal bone remodeling and density. It is considered less severe than the autosomal recessive form, but can still cause significant complications such as bone fractures and other skeletal abnormalities.
